hypothesis: A report generated directly from versioned CSV/JSON outputs can reproduce the validated numerical conclusions while remaining visually inspectable and rebuildable from one command.
limitations: The report faithfully documents the current effective paraxial model and does not upgrade it to an anatomical multi-surface eye.
Absolute retinal irradiance and biological safety remain outside scope because source radiometry, exposure, spectrum, and tissue transmission are not supplied.
The embedded SimSun font is a Windows system font, so rebuilding on another operating system requires a metrically appropriate Songti font substitution.
next_step: Collect measured radiometry and mechanical geometry, replace the effective thin lens with multi-surface anatomical eyes, and extend the OpticStudio validation to sequential aberration and non-sequential stray-light analyses.
objective: Generate and self-check a comprehensive Chinese SimSun LaTeX/PDF report for the completed chick, child, and adult 650 nm posterior-pole illumination simulation.
observations: The report contains an illustrative lens-system diagram and a separate reproducible-workflow diagram drawn as vector TikZ graphics.
Five quantitative figures are regenerated from validated result files with Chinese SimSun labels.
Automated PDF inspection passed, and manual visual review covered the cover, diagrams, equations, Monte Carlo heatmaps, OpticStudio comparison, long tables, conclusions, and references.
A long running header initially overlapped a chapter title; manual review caught it, the header was simplified, and the report was rebuilt successfully.
